Every package and its main modules, grouped by the machine it runs on. Arrows carry the engine numbers and how the call travels: HTTP on a local port, a started process, a file on disk, or a Python import. Hover or tap a block to read what it does.

Pick a blockIts job appears here.
Every block as a list
Owner's laptop 5
  • Claude Code — Claude Code sessions on the owner's laptop write the code. No models, no GPU, no product venv run here.
  • repo checkout — Git worktrees of github.com/AbdulrahmanAmer/nightshift; builders commit and push, CI does the testing.
  • tests/ — The test suite. Every heavy service is replaced by a fake that still writes real files (WAV, MP4, JSON).
  • dev/ — make_bundle.ps1 builds Nightshift-<ver>.zip; gate_m0 / gate_m3_* run whole pipelines on fakes; check_scope.py keeps builders inside their folders.
  • DEMO.cmd — Runs the dashboard UI with demo data on any PC that has Node, for design review.
GitHub 4
  • ci.yml — Runs on every push on windows-latest: lint, types, test (with fakes), ui-build, powershell-parse, bundle, scope-check.
  • release.yml — On a version tag: tests, builds Nightshift-<ver>.zip, nightshift-app-<ver>.zip and their .sha256, publishes the GitHub Release.
  • build-qwentts.yml — Builds the qwentts.cpp Windows CUDA binary and attaches qwentts-win-cuda-x64.zip (about 632 MB) to the release.
  • GitHub Releases — github.com/AbdulrahmanAmer/nightshift/releases: the bundle zip (3 MB), the app zip for ns update, and the qwentts binary.
installer 9
  • INSTALL.cmd 9 — Starts installer\stage1.ps1 with execution policy bypassed for that one process. -Ui / -NoUi pick window or headless.
  • stage1.ps1 9 — Probes the PC, gets uv and Python 3.12, starts the setup server and waits on it. Reopens the window if setup is already running.
  • stage2/web 9 fake in CI — installer.stage2.web: standard-library HTTP server. Owns the setup state, runs bootstrap steps b01-b03, starts the wizard as a child. CI runs it with --simulate.
  • installer/ui 9 — The setup screens (Vite build committed in installer/ui/static): Welcome, PC check, Choices, Download, Installing, Verify, Done, Uninstall.
  • wizard.py 9 — installer.stage2.wizard inside venvs\studio. Runs the steps and reports to P1 as JSON lines on stdin/stdout (--ui-bridge stdio).
  • steps s00-s10 9 — s00 welcome, s01 questions, s02 bins, s03 models, s04 venvs, s05 OpenCode, s06 tune, s07 configs, s08 smoke, s09 shortcuts + task, s10 summary, v01 samples.
  • downloader 9 fake in CI — installer.stage2.downloader: HTTP Range resume, SHA256 check, copies matching files from a local models_source folder instead of downloading.
  • manifest.json 9 — Repo root. Every model and binary with repo, file, revision and bytes: LLM tiers 9.0 / 14.3 / 22.9 GB, TTS 4.4 GB, whisper, llama.cpp b12032, qwentts, yt-dlp, WebView2, YuNet.
  • answers.json 9 — Optional, next to INSTALL.cmd. With it setup runs headless with no window and no questions; keys move to Credential Manager and config\secrets.dpapi (DPAPI, for the nightly task).
Windows 6
  • Task Scheduler 7 — Scheduled task registered by ns_supervisor.schedule: daily at run_time (default 03:00), WakeToRun, StartWhenAvailable. Runs studio run --daily. Logon S4U, else interactive only (NS-W205); the time is kept in config\schedule.json.
  • Desktop shortcuts 8 — Nightshift Dashboard, Studio, Code, Stop All, Update, Diagnostics, Open Outbox. Each runs a launcher script.
  • Job Object 7 — Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (ns_supervisor.procs). If the supervisor dies, every model process dies with it: no stuck VRAM.
  • nvidia-smi 7 — Read by ns_supervisor.gpu for the GPU meters (name, load, VRAM, temperature), cached so polling never spawns a process per request.
  • Toasts · notes 7 — ns_supervisor.notify.toast_or_note: a Windows toast (AppUserModelID Nightshift); without a desktop (the 03:00 run) a morning note in run\morning_note.json that the dashboard bell shows.
  • WebView2 window 8 — The frameless Nightshift window drawn by nightshift-host.ps1 around WebView2. Falls back to Edge or Chrome --app, then the default browser.
launchers 6
  • dashboard.ps1 8 — launchers\nightshift-dashboard.ps1: starts the supervisor if needed, waits for it and for :8100, then opens the host window.
  • stop-all.ps1 7 — launchers\stop-all.ps1: asks the supervisor to stop every model and exit.
  • host.ps1 8 — launchers\nightshift-host.ps1: single-instance frameless WPF window around WebView2. Closing it never stops the engine.
  • update.ps1 7 — launchers\update.ps1: steps out of the app folder, then runs ns update (GitHub release, a zip, or --git --channel stable|main) with rollback.
  • diagnostics.ps1 7 — launchers\diagnostics.ps1: ns doctor --bundle, writes nightshift-diagnostics-<date>.zip to the Desktop.
  • code.ps1 7 — launchers\nightshift-code.ps1: optional Nightshift Code; holds the LLM as owner opencode while the terminal is open.
ns_supervisor 15
  • app 7 — ns_supervisor.app: FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8099. /status, /acquire, /release, /heartbeat, /release_owner, /stop_all, /shutdown, /warmup, /events.
  • core 7 — ns_supervisor.core: GPU lock, tenant swap, health polling (500 ms, 120 s), crash policy, idle unload (10 min), auto-exit (30 min, or 60 s after POST /run_finished), weekly update check; reclaims a studio: GPU lease with no heartbeat for 10 minutes (a PC that slept does not count).
  • lock 7 — ns_supervisor.lock: first come first served, timeout per waiter, records the owner (studio:<job>, opencode, verify, gate).
  • procs 7 — ns_supervisor.procs: starts children with logs to logs\<service>-YYYYMMDD.jsonl, terminates them, Job Object, VRAM probe.
  • services 7 — ns_supervisor.services: service table from config\runtime.json: llama, embed, tts, dashboard; command line, port, health URL, GPU flag.
  • client 7 fake in CI — ns_supervisor.client: the real Acquirer the studio uses to ask for a service. ns_studio.acquirer.StudioAcquirer wraps it for studio run (starts the engine, waits 2 h for a busy GPU, POST /heartbeat every 30 s while it holds a service); CI keeps DevAcquirer.
  • schedule 7 — ns_supervisor.schedule: registers or removes the Nightshift Daily task through PowerShell.
  • scheduled 7 — ns_supervisor.scheduled: dashboard jobs set for a later time (schedule_at) are released when due.
  • notify 7 — ns_supervisor.notify: Windows toast at the end of a run or on failure.
  • cli (ns) 7 — ns_supervisor.cli: the ns tool: status, stop, verify, tune, doctor, update, backup, restore, schedule, notify, models get voicedesign|story_llm.
  • verify + tune 7 — ns_supervisor.verify and tune: health, completion, TTS, whisper, embed, NVENC and benchmarks; tune writes the fastest llama flags to runtime.json.
  • update 7 — ns_supervisor.update + update_job: a detached worker outside the engine's Job Object (CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB, else WMI) installs into <app_path>.new, swaps keeping .prev, re-syncs the venvs from ns_common.venv_extras and writes run\update_state.json. The worker runs from a private copy of venvs\supervisor (run\updater\venv-<stamp>) and, after the swap or a rollback, starts the engine again (and the dashboard window if one was open) and waits for /status before writing done.
  • doctor 7 — ns_supervisor.doctor: logs, install_state, runtime, verify-report, nvidia-smi, pip freeze, last 3 job folders. Never keys, models or videos.
  • backup 6 — ns_supervisor.backup: ns backup / restore: config, voice embeddings, studio.db, exemplars. No models or videos.
  • gpu 7 — ns_supervisor.gpu: cached nvidia-smi readout for Status.gpu.
ns_dashboard 20
  • server 8 — ns_dashboard.server: FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100, serves the built React UI from static/ and every /api route. Loopback only.
  • handlers 8 — ns_dashboard.handlers: the logic behind every /api route, free of the web framework.
  • svc_outputs 8 — Queue page: list, detail, approve, reject, mark uploaded (paste the YouTube link).
  • svc_jobs 8 — Create page: story runs, clip jobs (file or link), learn, verify; upload plumbing.
  • svc_library 6 — Library page: idea bank, stories, footage cache, formats.
  • svc_channels 6 — Channels page: create, edit, pause, resume, validate (distinctness warnings).
  • svc_voices 2 — Library > Voices: design a voice from a description or clone a 3-10 s sample (rights confirmed); a Pending voice from setup card (GET /api/voices/pending, POST /api/voices/apply-pending → studio_job apply_voice).
  • svc_settings 8 — Settings: keys (Credential Manager and config\secrets.dpapi, so the 03:00 run sees a changed key), engine flags as dotted keys, diagnostics, models get, logs, learn summary (top, bottom, daily, milestone).
  • svc_engine 7 — Engine pill and /api/status: warm-up, quit, GPU meters, next run time, schedule_registered (false: No nightly task), Release the GPU (POST /api/engine/release_gpu).
  • jobs 7 — ns_dashboard.jobs: table dashboard_jobs and one FIFO worker thread; jobs carry step/steps; on_recover frees an interrupted series part, on_idle answers saved Assistant requests.
  • uploads 8 — Resumable chunked uploads into imports\clipper\<source_id>\.
  • studio_runner 7 fake in CI — ns_dashboard.studio_runner starts venvs\studio python -m ns_dashboard.studio_job <kind> --args <file>; the child runs studio_bridge (run_job_guarded, create/resume_clip_job, series parts, import_url) and prints NSJOB JSON lines. Kinds: run, clip, rerun, series, download, transcribe, apply_voice. Cancel: a flag file checked between stages, then procs.kill_tree, then release_owner for its studio: owners. Fakes in CI.
  • supervisor_link 7 — Loopback client the dashboard uses for /status, /acquire, /events, warm-up and quit.
  • media 8 — Range (206) streaming of output MP4s so the player can seek; cached thumbnails.
  • updater 7 — Settings > Update: ns update --check / --github, then follows run\update_state.json across the restart; Settings > Models runs ns models get.
  • events 8 — Thread-safe pub/sub and server-sent events for live progress.
  • assistant 8 fake in CI — ns_dashboard.assistant: tool-calling loop on the local Qwen; every state-changing action waits for a Yes on a confirm card. Scripted fake LLM in CI.
  • registry + tools 8 — Every /api route declares a tool descriptor or is listed as no-tool; a hygiene test fails CI otherwise.
  • orientation 8 — system_map, find, where_is, search_docs (BM25 over the docs), explain_error.
  • ui (React) 8 — ns_dashboard/ui: React + Vite, ref12 card language; built into ns_dashboard/static and committed. No CDN, works offline.
GPU tenants + tools 12
  • llama-server 1 fake in CI — llama.cpp b12032 CUDA build serving the model picked in setup (Balanced Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MTP 14.3 GB by default, MoE layers partly on CPU) with aliases code,story. CI: FakeLlm.
  • embed 1 fake in CI — llama-server --embeddings with nomic-embed-text v1.5 Q8_0 (146 MB) on CPU, never locked. Started with -c 2048 -b 2048 -ub 2048; callers send a token-aware window of whole sentences up to 480 tokens. CI: FakeEmbed counts tokens the same way.
  • ns_tts server 2 fake in CI — ns_tts.server: FastAPI TTS service, supervisor venv for qwentts and venvs\tts for the PyTorch engine; batch speech endpoint (all chunks with one voice, language and speed go to one qwen-tts process); /health reports engine_kind. CI: FakeTts tone bursts.
  • ns_tts engine 2 — ns_tts.engine: qwentts.cpp engine, or the PyTorch reference engine when the smoke test fails (NS-W301).
  • qwen-tts.exe 2 — bin\qwentts: qwen-tts.exe renders one chunk (text on stdin, --speaker or --ref-spk/--ref-rvq/--ref-text, -o WAV); qwen-codec.exe encodes a new voice. tts-server.exe ships unused.
  • voices 2 — ns_tts.voices: models\tts\voices\<name>\ with voice.json (files) + speaker.spk + speaker.rvq + ref.txt; PyTorch voices keep speaker.bin. The other engine refuses them (NS-E311).
  • faster-whisper 3 fake in CI — distil-large-v3 int8 (about 1.5 GB) loaded inside the studio process or the dashboard's studio-venv child under the GPU lock and dropped on release; no server. CI: FakeTranscriber.
  • ffmpeg 4 fake in CI — FFmpeg (winget). h264_nvenc on the RTX card, libx264 fallback (NS-W401). CI: libx264 ultrafast.
  • yt-dlp 4 — Pinned yt-dlp.exe (2026.10.26) in bin\yt-dlp, used by the Clipper to fetch a video from a link.
  • OpenCV YuNet 4 — cv2.FaceDetectorYN with the pinned YuNet ONNX: faces and facecam for the Clipper layouts.
  • spaCy 2 — en_core_web_md sentencizer used to split narration into sentences before TTS chunking.
  • OpenCode 7 — Optional coding agent (v1.19.5) pointed at the local LLM; holds the GPU as owner opencode.
ns_studio 25
  • cli (studio) 7 — ns_studio.cli: studio run, clip, series, ask, status, voice, calibrate.
  • daily 7 — ns_studio.daily: the nightly run planned by the cadence governor per active channel, with a DB backup at the end.
  • jobs 7 — ns_studio.jobs: creates or resumes a job, wires real or fake services, inserts the policy gates into the plan.
  • orchestrator 7 — ns_studio.orchestrator: canonical stage order per format (shorts_only, master_first, master_from_script, clip); runs stages grouped by GPU tenant.
  • stages 7 — ns_studio.stages: stage protocol and registry; a stage is skipped when its outputs exist and inputs are unchanged, so a crash resumes.
  • context 7 — ns_studio.context: the job folder data\jobs\<job_id>\ and service wiring handed to every stage.
  • text 1 fake in CI — ns_studio.text: stages_master, stages_shorts, seo, validators, word budgets. Calls the LLM; CI uses FakeLlm fixtures.
  • variation 1 — ns_studio.variation: draws the combo (hook, structure, pacing, caption style...) from the channel's pools using pool_weights; each Short gets its own combo; pacing sets the TTS speed.
  • policy 5 fake in CI — ns_studio.policy: policy_text after the text stages, policy_final before outbox; rule checks, LLM judge, perceptual hashes.
  • review 6 — ns_studio.review: review queue, mark uploaded, pause and resume a channel.
  • media/voice 2 fake in CI — ns_studio.media.voice: one batch call to the TTS service at the pacing speed (ns_common.pacing), per-item loudness normalisation, script sidecars.
  • media/transcribe 3 fake in CI — ns_studio.media.transcribe: Transcriber protocol, faster-whisper engine (in-process, GPU) and the fake.
  • media/captions 3 — ns_studio.media.captions: aligns whisper words to the script's words in any script, gates on the caption-to-speech offset, builds ASS subtitles with the contrast fallback.
  • media/clips 4 fake in CI — ns_studio.media.clips + clip_sources: keyword dedupe, Pexels and Pixabay search with rate limits, 90-day cache, reuse rules.
  • media/render 4 fake in CI — ns_studio.media.render, longform, layout: FFmpeg filter graphs; h264_nvenc on the GPU PC, libx264 ultrafast in CI.
  • media/qc 5 — ns_studio.media.qc: duration, loudness, caption drift, black frames, file opens, hook timing, aspect.
  • media/outbox 6 — ns_studio.media.outbox: files into outbox\<channel>\... (paths under 200 characters), upload sheets (.json + .txt, with the time zone), outputs rows, <job>\outbox\manifest.json for the publish slots.
  • clipper 4 fake in CI — ns_studio.clipper: import (file or yt-dlp link, CancelToken), analyze (display rotation), one whisper pass, select + judge, layout, captions, render, clip SEO rules, QC, outbox; a failing clip is skipped.
  • series 1 — ns_studio.series: story folders under stories\<slug>\, workshop tools, script_import stage; parts carry their design, title, Part N of M, end card and publish delay.
  • learn 6 — ns_studio.learn: imports the YouTube Studio CSV, reweights pool_weights, builds the status report.
  • channels 6 — ns_studio.channels: channel profiles and the cadence governor (how many masters and Shorts per week).
  • calibrate 5 — ns_studio.calibrate: compares critic scores with ratings to recommend the critic bar.
  • prompts/ 1 — ns_studio/prompts: the prompt files (plan, draft, critic, revise, SEO, visual plan, clip_select, clip_judge, policy_check...).
  • media/shotplan 4 — ns_studio.media.shotplan: beats to time spans to shot slots shared by clips and render.
  • media/thumbnails 4 — ns_studio.media.thumbnails: high-contrast frame pick plus short Pillow text layouts.
ns_common + contracts 12
  • models — ns_common.models: every data shape in one place; contracts/schemas must equal its JSON schema.
  • config + paths — ns_common.config and paths: where everything lives under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Nightshift (or the chosen home), runtime.json loading; also secrets_names, secret_file (DPAPI), venv_extras, uv.find_uv, pacing.
  • db 6 — ns_common.db: the SQLite access layer over contracts/schema.sql.
  • llm_client 1 — ns_common.llm_client: complete_json / complete_text against llama-server.
  • tts_client 2 — ns_common.tts_client: speak / speak_batch against the TTS service; failures are NS-E310 / E311 / E315.
  • embed_client 1 — ns_common.embed_client: embeddings for idea dedupe and policy checks; embed_window keeps whole sentences up to 480 tokens, counted per script (Latin ~4 chars a token, Cyrillic 2.5, CJK 1); failures are NS-E316.
  • acquire 7 — ns_common.acquire: the Acquirer protocol (acquire / release a service).
  • ffmpeg 4 — ns_common.ffmpeg: FFmpeg and ffprobe invocation helpers.
  • errors + logging — ns_common.errors and logging: coded errors from contracts/errors.json and JSONL logs.
  • contracts/schemas — contracts/schemas: JSON schemas generated from ns_common.models (answers, story, plans, upload sheets...).
  • errors.json — contracts/errors.json: every NS-E / NS-W code with a plain message and a fix hint.
  • schema.sql 6 — contracts/schema.sql: channels, runs, ideas, stories, parts, clips, clip_usage, outputs, uploads, analytics, pool_weights, dashboard_jobs, assistant tables...
NIGHTSHIFT_HOME on disk 16
  • models\llm 1 — One GGUF: Small Qwen3-14B 9.0 GB, Balanced Qwen3.6-35B-A3B APEX MTP 14.3 GB (default), Best 22.9 GB, or the owner's Hugging Face GGUF.
  • models\tts 2 — CustomVoice 2.04 GB + Base 2.08 GB talkers + tokenizer 0.29 GB; VoiceDesign 2.04 GB through ns models get; PyTorch checkouts in hf\ when the fallback runs.
  • models\whisper 3 — faster-distil-whisper-large-v3 (Systran).
  • bin\ 9 — llama.cpp + cudart, qwentts, uv, yt-dlp, WebView2 runtime DLLs, OpenCode if chosen.
  • venvs\ 9 — Python 3.12 environments built with uv from uv.lock; a tts venv only when the PyTorch fallback is needed.
  • config\ 7 — runtime.json (service flags), install_state.json (+ .bak), channels\, schedule.json (run time of a registered task only; a refused task keeps the time in dashboard.json), secrets.dpapi (API keys), pending_voice.json.
  • data\studio.db 6 — Everything Nightshift remembers: channels, ideas, stories, outputs, clip_usage, uploads, analytics, pool_weights, dashboard_jobs.
  • data\assistant.db 8 — Assistant conversations, messages and pending confirm actions.
  • data\jobs\ 7 — Working folder per job: stage_state.json and every stage's files (idea.json, story.json, audio\, words\, clips\, long\, shorts\, qc\).
  • cache\clips 4 — Downloaded stock clips with metadata; cache hits cost no API call.
  • outbox\ 6 — Finished videos by content: stories\<title>\full|shorts, series\<series>\part-NN\, clips\<source>\, each with an upload sheet.
  • rejected\ 5 — Anything that failed QC or a policy gate, with the reason.
  • stories\ 1 — Series Workshop folders: concept.md, series.md, design.yaml, status.yaml, parts\part-NN\.
  • imports\ 6 — Uploaded source videos for the Clipper and the YouTube Studio CSV exports.
  • logs\ 7 — One JSONL log per service per day.
  • models\embed·cv 1 — nomic-embed-text v1.5 and the YuNet face model; spaCy model in models\spacy.
Internet 6
  • Hugging Face 9 fake in CI — Public repos, no token: Qwen/Qwen3-14B-GGUF, Serveurperso/Qwen3-TTS-GGUF, Systran/faster-distil-whisper-large-v3, nomic-embed. CI simulates downloads.
  • GitHub downloads 9 fake in CI — llama.cpp releases, qwentts release asset, uv, yt-dlp, OpenCode; WebView2 from NuGet; YuNet from opencv_zoo.
  • Pexels API 4 fake in CI — Stock video search and download, client limit 180 per hour. CI: FakeClipSource makes testsrc2 clips.
  • Pixabay API 4 fake in CI — Stock video search and download, client limit 90 per minute, searches cached 24 h.
  • YouTube (link) 4 — A video the owner has rights to, fetched by link for the Clipper.
  • YouTube Studio 6 — The owner uploads by hand from the Outbox and exports the analytics CSV that feeds the learning loop.

The nine engines

The same modules, grouped by job. The numbers are used on every arrow in this page.

1

Story engine

Picks or invents an idea, plans the chapters, writes, critiques and revises the story. Then writes titles, descriptions, tags and the visual plan for every beat.

Made of
  • llama-server (llama.cpp b12032, CUDA) on :8080
  • model picked in setup: Balanced Qwen3.6-35B-A3B APEX MTP 14.3 GB (default from 32 GB RAM), Small Qwen3-14B 9.0 GB, Best 22.9 GB, or any Hugging Face GGUF
  • nomic-embed-text v1.5 Q8_0, 146 MB, CPU :8081 (idea dedupe)
  • ns_studio/text, prompts/, exemplars/, variation, series
In → out
channel profile, idea bank, pool weights → idea.json, plan.json, story.json, seo_long.json, visual_plan.json, shorts_plan.json
Runs on
Partner PC GPU. CI: FakeLlm fixtures
Talks to
7 6 5 2
2

Voice engine

Reads the script aloud in the channel's voice, all sentences in one batch. Stitches the pieces with set pauses and evens out the loudness.

Made of
  • qwen-tts.exe and qwen-codec.exe from the qwentts.cpp CUDA zip (632 MB): one --stream-by-line process per batch of chunks that share voice, language and speed, text on stdin, --lang from the channel language
  • CustomVoice talker 2.04 GB + Base talker 2.08 GB + tokenizer 0.29 GB = 4.4 GB
  • VoiceDesign 2.04 GB: ns models get voicedesign follows runtime.tts.engine (GGUF talker, or the Hugging Face weights for the PyTorch engine)
  • ns_tts (server :8091, engine, voices, audio), spaCy sentences
  • speed from the combo's pacing (0.7–1.3), FFmpeg atempo, pitch kept
  • PyTorch reference engine in venvs\tts as fallback (NS-W301)
  • voice_setup: the voice chosen in setup, made by the first job that runs or by Library > Voices > Create it now (studio_job apply_voice)
In → out
story.json sentences + cliff lines + pacing speed → audio\<id>.wav per chapter and per Short hook
Runs on
Partner PC GPU. CI: FakeTts tone bursts
Talks to
1 7 3

Ear

Listens to the narration, or to the owner's video, and times every word. Lines the captions up with the script's own spelling.

Made of

  • ns_studio/media/transcribe, media/captions
  • clipper/transcribe_stage

WAV → words\<id>.json, captions\<id>.ass (median caption-to-speech offset ≤ 120 ms, else NS-E403; whisper failure NS-E408)
Runs on

Picture engine

Turns the visual plan into shots: finds footage, picks clips under reuse rules, lays out the frame. Renders the master and the Shorts with FFmpeg and makes the thumbnails.

Made of
  • Pexels and Pixabay APIs (free keys from Credential Manager, else config\secrets.dpapi), cache\clips for 90 days
  • the owner's own video or a YouTube link via yt-dlp (Clipper, cancellable)
  • OpenCV YuNet faces and facecam (Clipper layouts)
  • media/shotplan, clips, layout, render, longform, derive, thumbnails
  • FFmpeg h264_nvenc, libx264 fallback
In → out
visual plan + audio + captions → long\master.mp4, shorts\s<k>\short.mp4, thumb_1..3.jpg, clips\c<k>.mp4

Judge

Stops anything that is not fit to post. Checks length, loudness, captions, black frames and policy rules, and judges each clip before it is rendered.

Made of
  • media/qc (qc.json targets)
  • policy: policy_text before voice (embeds a token-aware opening window, whole sentences up to 480 tokens), policy_final before outbox
  • critic scores in the text stages; tag_relevance asks the model
  • clipper judge_loop (clip_judge prompt)
  • calibrate (critic bar)
In → out
text and rendered files → qc.json, policy_text.json, policy_final.json; failures go to rejected\

Conductor

Decides what runs when, and lets only one big model hold the GPU at a time. Starts, stops and cleans up every process, and resumes a job after a crash.

Made of
  • ns_supervisor: app :8099, core, lock, procs + Job Object, services, schedule + schedule.json, notify (toast or morning note), verify, tune, update_job (detached, from a private venv copy, relaunches the engine) + update_check (weekly), models get, doctor, backup; studio: GPU leases renewed by /heartbeat, reclaimed after 10 silent minutes
  • ns_studio: acquirer (StudioAcquirer, 30 s heartbeat thread), orchestrator (embed lease), stages (stage_state.json), jobs, daily (toast, run_finished), cli
  • Task Scheduler Nightshift Daily, 03:00, WakeToRun
In → out
a job request → stages in order, GPU tenant swaps, logs

Installer

Takes a clean PC to a working studio in about an hour. Checks the PC, asks the choices (model picker included), downloads 16–21 GB, verifies, creates the shortcuts and the 03:00 task.

Made of
  • INSTALL.cmd → stage1.ps1 (hands uv over in NIGHTSHIFT_BOOTSTRAP_UV) → stage2/web (P1) + installer/ui
  • wizard.py (P2) with steps s00–s10; s08 checks local/code after s07
  • downloader: resumable, SHA256, 60 s stall abort, pause inside the stream
  • manifest.json, answers.json (llm_tier, llm_custom, include_voicedesign)
  • keys into Credential Manager and config\secrets.dpapi; task S4U, else interactive (NS-W205)
In → out
zip + answers → NIGHTSHIFT_HOME (models, bin, venvs, config), shortcuts, task, diagnostics zip
Runs on
Partner PC. CI: --simulate downloads
Talks to
7 + smoke tests of 1–4

Plumbing

The wire level, read from the code. Numbered squares are steps in order; filled circles are engine numbers; dashed boxes use a fake in CI. Open one panel at a time.

Ports and start-upWhich process starts which, on which port
ProcessPortWhat it speaksStarted by
ns_supervisor.app8099HTTP: /health /status /acquire /release /heartbeat /release_owner /stop_all /shutdown /warmup, GET+POST /events (SSE)launcher or Task Scheduler (_common.ps1:55)
ns_dashboard.server8100React UI at /, JSON under /api, SSE for events and Assistant chatsupervisor, as a persistent non-GPU service (services.py:124)
llama-server.exe8080OpenAI-style POST /v1/chat/completions (JSON schema in response_format), GET /healthsupervisor on /acquire llama
llama-server.exe --embeddings8081POST /v1/embeddings, CPU only, never lockedsupervisor on /acquire embed
ns_tts.server8091POST /v1/audio/speech/batch, /v1/audio/speech, /v1/voices, /v1/voices/design, /v1/voices/clonesupervisor on /acquire tts (venvs\tts python for the PyTorch engine, services.py:117); it runs one qwen-tts.exe --stream-by-line process per batch of chunks
faster-whispernonePython library inside the process that runs the jobthe supervisor only lends the GPU lock (core.py:351)
  • Process tree: the supervisor puts every child in one Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (procs.py:103); breakaway is allowed so ns update can leave it (update_job.py:36). If the supervisor ends, llama-server, ns_tts and the dashboard end with it.
  • Update: the detached worker runs from a private copy of venvs\supervisor (run\updater\venv-<stamp>, ns_supervisor/updater_copy.py) so uv can rewrite the real venv. It notes whether the engine and a dashboard window were running, and after the swap (or a rollback) starts them again and waits for /status before it writes done; an engine that does not come back is failed with restart_failed (ns_supervisor/relaunch.py).
  • Children start with CREATE_NO_WINDOW; their output goes to logs\<service>-YYYYMMDD.jsonl (procs.py:206).
  • Spec and code differ: the spec has qwentts serving :8091 itself; in the code ns_tts.server is always the server and starts qwen-tts.exe for each chunk with the text on stdin (ns_tts/engine.py:290-322). tts-server.exe ships in the zip but is not used: it holds one talker and its voices only in RAM. Batching: every chunk of a request that shares voice, language and speed goes to ONE qwen-tts --stream-by-line -o - process, one line per chunk, and the WAVs are cut apart on their RIFF headers (ns_tts/engine.py:404-444, ns_tts/audio.py). One failing chunk fails the whole request.
  • Dashboard jobs (Run now, clips, re-runs, series parts, link downloads, the clone transcript, the pending setup voice) run in a child: venvs\studio\Scripts\python.exe -m ns_dashboard.studio_job <kind> --args <file> with cwd = app folder and NIGHTSHIFT_HOME set; progress comes back as NSJOB {json} lines (ns_dashboard/studio_runner.py, studio_job.py:38). Cancel creates the flag file named in NS_JOB_CANCEL_FILE, which the child checks before each stage (10 s grace; a link download also cancels its CancelToken, 3 s), then kills the tree and sends POST /release_owner for every studio:<job> owner (adapters.py:239-319).
GPU tenant swapacquire → lock → unload → spawn → health → work + heartbeat → release → idle → exit
TenantModel on diskOn the GPU
llama-server :8080Balanced Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MTP, 14.3 GB (Small 9.0, Best 22.9)ctx 16384 (ns_common/models.py:84); Balanced and Best keep 8 or 12 MoE layers on the CPU, q8_0 KV cache and MTP drafting (installer/stage2/runtime_cfg.py:43-50); Small is fully on the GPU. The code has no VRAM budget, it only measures.
ns_tts + qwen-tts :8091talker 2.0 GB + tokenizer 0.3 GB per voice typeloaded once per batch by one qwen-tts.exe --stream-by-line process; not measured in the code
faster-whisperdistil-large-v3 int8, about 1.5 GBloaded for the captions stage and unloaded when its tenant is released
embed :8081nomic-embed v1.5, 146 MBCPU only, outside the lock; started with -c 2048 -b 2048 -ub 2048 (embed_server_args, services.py:110)
  • Why one at a time: the LLM alone takes most of a 16 GB card, so the TTS talker or whisper would not fit beside it. The orchestrator groups consecutive stages by tenant so each model loads once per run (orchestrator.py:126).
  • Lease: a studio: owner renews its hold with POST /heartbeat every 30 s from a thread in StudioAcquirer, so an hour-long stage still beats (ns_studio/acquirer.py:133-167). A studio: lease silent for 10 minutes is reclaimed with release_owner (lock, queue place and embed); a monitor pass more than 60 s late means the PC slept and restarts the clock, and a model still loading is not silence (ns_supervisor/core.py:420-480). Other owners (the Assistant, previews, ns verify) never expire. The Queue shows GPU held by … with a Release button (POST /api/engine/release_gpu).
  • Crash policy: 3 crashes within 10 minutes put the service in error and jobs fail with NS-E202 (core.py:194, :304).
  • Who asks: studio run (and the 03:00 run) builds StudioAcquirer (ns_studio/acquirer.py:51, ns_studio/context.py:89), which starts the engine if it is down and waits up to 2 h for a busy GPU, then stops with NS-E201 and lists the rest as skipped. Stages that embed text hold embed while they run (orchestrator.py:96) and send a token-aware window: whole sentences up to 480 tokens, counted per script and capped at 90 % of -b (ns_common/embed_client.py:64-84). The run ends with POST /run_finished (daily.py:153).
Story engine internalsprompt file → schema-bound JSON → critic gate
  • Output is constrained by a JSON schema sent in response_format (llama.cpp turns it into a grammar on the server side); the code does not send GBNF itself. After parsing it is validated against the pydantic model; a validation failure is not retried (llm_client.py:46-82).
  • Temperature 0.8 for every story prompt; a regenerated job changes seed, temperature and clips. Prompt files in <home>\prompt_overrides win over the shipped ones (prompts.py:221). Thinking is switched per prompt by its front-matter (chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking). Context window 16384 tokens.
  • Hard validators run after the critic: sentence ≤ 35 words, opening line not too close to past openings (cosine 0.8), cliff lines varied (text/validators.py).
  • Master-first runs the critic per chapter, then a continuity pass. Prompt versions are saved per job, and --resume no longer redoes LLM stages after the voice stage. Each Short gets its own combo (hook, caption look, pacing).
Voice engine internalschunk → batch synthesis → stitch → loudness
  • Pauses: 120 ms when a long sentence was split, 350 ms between sentences, 700 ms at a paragraph or chapter break, 1200 ms before a cliff line (ns_tts/audio.py:23-26). Speed is pacing_speed (voice speed × the pacing's words per minute, clamped 0.7–1.3, ns_common/pacing.py:12), applied as an FFmpeg atempo chain so the pitch stays.
  • Voice sources: 9 built-in CustomVoice speakers (Ryan, Aiden, Vivian, Serena, Uncle_Fu, Dylan, Eric, Ono_Anna, Sohee); a designed voice (VoiceDesign talker, turned once into an embedding); a cloned voice from a 3-10 s sample (ns_tts/voices.py).
  • Stored voices live in models\tts\voices\<name>\: qwentts voices as voice.json (with files), speaker.spk, speaker.rvq and ref.txt; PyTorch voices as speaker.bin. Each engine refuses the other's voices with NS-E311 (ns_tts/engine.py:34-38).
  • New voices: a clone runs qwen-codec.exe -i speaker.wav; a design renders a sample with the VoiceDesign talker --instruct and encodes it the same way. Without that talker the answer is NS-E314, fixed by ns models get voicedesign, which follows runtime.tts.engine: the GGUF talker for qwentts, the Hugging Face VoiceDesign (and Base) weights in models\tts\hf for the PyTorch engine (ns_supervisor/models_get.py:65-84). The language of every request is the channel's, mapped to a --lang name (ns_common/languages.py; unknown is English with a warning).
  • A voice designed or cloned in setup waits in config\pending_voice.json. The first job that runs makes it (run_job_guarded calls apply_pending_voices first, ns_studio/policy/regen.py:146), or the owner presses Create it now in Library > Voices (POST /api/voices/apply-pending → studio_job apply_voice).
  • Fallback: if the qwentts smoke test fails at install, the PyTorch reference engine runs in venvs\tts from models\tts\hf (NS-W301, also reported by ns verify from /health engine_kind). CI uses FakeTts and a strict stand-in for the two executables.
Ear and captionsword timestamps → alignment → ASS → burn-in
  • Model settings come from runtime.json: setup writes distil-large-v3 on cuda, int8, like the code default and the spec (installer/stage2/runtime_cfg.py:41). Drift is the median offset between caption and speech word starts, so speech rhythm alone no longer fails NS-E403 (captions.py:140). CI uses FakeTranscriber, which reads the script sidecars the voice stage wrote.
  • The mask changes only the caption text, never the audio.
Picture engine internalsbeats → footage → filter graph → NVENC
  • Clipper layouts: YuNet (cv2.FaceDetectorYN, score ≥ 0.8, 640 px) finds faces and a facecam; the model picks the layout per clip and the detection rules are the fallback (clipper/detect.py, stages_clip.py:419).
  • Output flags: yuv420p, AAC 192k 48 kHz mono, +faststart. CI encodes with libx264 ultrafast and FakeClipSource makes testsrc2 clips; FakeFaceDetector stands in for YuNet.
Jobs and datajobs table → worker → job folder → outbox → review → learn
FileWhereWho reads it
studio.dbNIGHTSHIFT_HOME\data\studio.dbstudio, dashboard, learn (paths.py:100)
assistant.dbNIGHTSHIFT_HOME\data\assistant.dbdashboard assistant store
runtime.jsonNIGHTSHIFT_HOME\config\runtime.jsonsupervisor services, studio context, tune writes it
install_state.jsonNIGHTSHIFT_HOME\config\installer resume, doctor (atomic, with .bak)
schedule.jsonNIGHTSHIFT_HOME\config\ns schedule writes it only when Windows registered the task (a refused task keeps the time in dashboard.json); /api/status sends schedule_registered = the file exists, and the top bar says No nightly task when it is false (s09_shortcuts_scheduler.py:77-83, svc_engine.py:156)
secrets.dpapiNIGHTSHIFT_HOME\config\setup and Settings > Keys write it next to Credential Manager (ns_dashboard/adapters.py:533-593); the studio reads it when Credential Manager has no key or its backend raises (ns_studio/jobs.py:84-121)
update_state.jsonNIGHTSHIFT_HOME\run\the detached updater writes it atomically; a dead worker pid reads as failed (effective_status); Settings > Updates follows it, then waits for /status on the new version
pending_voice.jsonNIGHTSHIFT_HOME\config\setup writes it; GET /api/voices/pending shows it until the voice exists
morning_note.jsonNIGHTSHIFT_HOME\run\notify.toast_or_note writes it; the bell and Last night show it (svc_engine.py:235)
manifest.jsonrepo root (app_path)ns_common/config.py:91, wizard, setup plan
  • Job kinds: run, clip, learn, verify and series_part (ns_dashboard/jobs.py:22). The worker hands run, clip and series_part to the studio-venv child (child kinds also include download, transcribe and apply_voice), where studio_bridge.py runs story jobs through policy.regen.run_job_guarded, clips through create_clip_job / resume_clip_job and series parts from the workshop's rows; tests/test_dashboard_wiring.py resolves every name it takes.
  • One Outbox layout: outbox\<channel>\stories\<title>\full|shorts (outbox.py:94). Each job lists its files in <job>\outbox\manifest.json; the cadence step reads it and rewrites both sheets with the slot, plus a series part's publish delay (daily.py:30-60).
Assistant plumbingchat → local LLM → tool registry → confirm card → result
  • Tools call the dashboard's handler objects directly in the same process, not over HTTP; the route on each descriptor ties it to its /api route for the hygiene test (assistant/tools.py, registry.py:70).
  • Approve and reject are never tools. The page words its cards from GET /api/assistant/tools. The Assistant is one fixed chat page with a History drawer (GET /assistant/conversations, /assistant/history) and replays requests saved while the engine was busy (POST /assistant/queue/run). Series Workshop tools are mounted with Yes/No cards (assistant/tools.py:382). CI drives the loop with a scripted fake LLM.

The last column, Verified on the partner PC, is empty on purpose: every cell says pending first run until the first real run on the partner's GPU PC. Nothing here was run (no model, no Python, no tests); the column's note says what that run must confirm for the row, and a dash means the run cannot settle it.
